newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria 98/99 budget missing 20 bln ATS - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Austria 98/99 budget missing 20 bln ATS - finmin.

text.p: Austria's budget for 1998 and 1999 is missing a total 20 billion schillings ($1.7 billion), Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger told a newspaper on Sunday, but added there was no plan to raise taxes on oil and tobacco to cover the gap.

In an interview with the daily Kurier, Edlinger said a Saturday newspaper report which claimed he was considering raising taxes on oil and tobacco to help fill the 25 billion schilling hole in the next budget, was "an incorrect report".
"That much (25 billion) is not needed. In truth, we need to bring in revenues of around 10 billion schillings each for 1998 and 1999. That is a perfectly bearable sum," Edlinger said.

The government would "certainly not target those taxes where a hike would prove counterproductive", he added. A higher oil tax would drive Austrians to fill up abroad, while increased tobacco tax would encourage cigarette smuggling, he said.
"One has to think about other areas," the finance minister said without elaborating.
Edlinger said the government was well on the way to having the 1998/99 budgets ready for the beginning of July. ($ = 11.91 Austrian Schillings)
